handoffs.message: EX-002 ready for review. Canonical rollback_action_type now stays in replace/pause_then_replace/liquidate_then_replace vocabulary through deployment_saga compensation, with legacy replace_binding normalized only at the compatibility boundary. Updated rollback policy, runtime-manager rollback matrix, and artifact-loader contract so cutover semantics use replacement RuntimeBinding creation/retire rather than in-place mutation, and loader validates fallback metadata without inventing rollback execution semantics. Verification: PYTHONPATH=services/control-plane/governance python3 -m unittest services/control-plane/governance/test_deployment_saga.py (9 tests), PYTHONPATH=services/control-plane/governance python3 -m unittest services/control-plane/governance/test_deployment_plan.py (24 tests), python3 services/control-plane/governance/smoke_test_deployment_saga.py (13/13), python3 services/execution/runtime-manager/smoke_test_runtime_binding.py (10/10 groups), python3 -m unittest services/execution/test_artifact_loader.py (9 tests), plus py_compile pass.

EX-002 approved. ROLLBACK_AND_POSITION_SEMANTICS.md locked as L1, rollback_action_matrix.md has explicit 3-action mapping (replace/pause_then_replace/liquidate_then_replace) with position treatment and telemetry cutover semantics. Legacy replace_binding normalized only at compatibility boundary in deployment_plan.py. Loader restricted to fallback metadata validation only. All tests pass: 9 saga, 24 plan, 13/13 smoke, 10/10 binding, 9/9 loader. Review at services/execution/review_ex002_claude_approved_zh.md.
